boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Fair Garden record (January 27, 1864) in Operations about Dandridge [December 1863-January 1864]. The January 26 skirmishes and the January 28 fight near Indian Creek with Armstrong's division, which the live description includes, fall outside the frozen date and are context only. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field names a cavalry division on each side without counts; the live field reads zero. Sturgis says Wolford's division numbered at most 900 men, that the victory of the 27th was won by La Grange's and Campbell's brigades of McCook's division alone, and on the 26th that the enemy was evidently very strong. Longstreet says the Union cavalry had been greatly increased from Chattanooga and calls it a superior force.
claims.rationale: Partial and qualitative statements; no matched count is inspected and none is adopted. The live zero is not measured absence.

NPS says the attack was made in a heavy fog.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Sturgis says the enemy was entirely routed about 4 p.m. after being driven all day. Longstreet says Martin was driven back 4 miles. NPS says McCook's men routed the Confederates. The next day, outside the frozen date, Longstreet reports a successful fight by Armstrong's cavalry and Sturgis withdrew from the area.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The later withdrawal is campaign context, not part of the frozen result.

claims.value: The frozen and live casualty texts read 265 (US 100; CS 165). Sturgis's February 4 report says his loss in the engagements of the 26th to 28th would not exceed 100 and the enemy's would not fall short of 400, and gives about 150 prisoners and 2 rifled 10-pounder guns; his evening dispatch of the 27th says over 100 prisoners, 2 pieces of 3-inch steel artillery and some 50 or 60 killed and wounded in the charge alone. Longstreet says Martin lost 200 killed, wounded and missing and 2 pieces of artillery.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Sturgis's 100 spans three days and is an upper estimate; his prisoner and gun descriptions differ between the dispatch and the report.

open_questions: McCook's, Campbell's, La Grange's, Lilly's, Garrard's and Savage's reports and Foster's telegrams (read, not selected) remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Sturgis's dispatches and reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volumes XXXI Part 1 and XXXII Part 1, are one family of interested Union accounts; Longstreet's telegrams, printed in Volume XXXII Part 1, are is a separate family of interested Confederate accounts. The volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
